risk_if_not_implemented: Without AI & Autonomous Technologies Mission and Goals Definition, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Failure to Achieve Strategic / Mission Objectives (R-EX-8), Failure to Support Business / Mission Objectives (R-GV-1), and most likely increases susceptibility to Dysfunctional Management Practices (MT-8), Human Error (MT-9).

compensating_control_1.name: Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Autonomous Technologies Governance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to ensure policies, processes, procedures and practices related to the mapping, measuring and managing of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Autonomous Technologies (AAT)-related risks are in place, transparent and implemented effectively.
compensating_control_1.justification: Artificial Intelligence (AI) & Autonomous Technologies Governance (AAT-02) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Mission and Goals Definition (AAT-03) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Defining Business Context & Mission
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to document the organization's business model and mission.
compensating_control_2.justification: Defining Business Context & Mission (GOV-06) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Mission and Goals Definition (AAT-03) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
